topic: Cycle-rank efficiency frontier for proportional staggered difference-in-differences. In a fixed-T staggered panel with independent units, arbitrary within-unit dependence and finite fourth moments, impose no anticipation and a positive connected multiplicative rank-one untreated-mean array mu_gt=a_g b_t. Target Moreau-Kastler's proportional treatment on the treated, theta_PTT=A/B-1. On the untreated cohort-time bipartite graph H_U let q=|U|-|C_U|-|T_U|+1. Prove that weighted alternating even-cycle vectors span the complete tangent restriction space, derive the canonical gradient and an attaining feasible covariance-weighted estimator, and differentiate the published PPML-imputation estimator. The hard theorem is topology-level: PPML imputation is efficient for every legal bounded nonnegative-outcome covariance law iff q=0. If q>0, show the universally efficient covariances satisfy exactly q independent primitive alternating balance equations, form a proper lower-dimensional subset, and construct an open realizable covariance family on which the exact loss Gamma=b'(R'Omega R)^(-1)b is strictly positive, with the sharp quadratic/spectral characterization and pointwise Wald inference. Keep the banked population PPML forbidden-comparison theorem and routine sandwich theory out of scope. Consumers are the Nagengast--Yotov regional-trade-agreement and Menkhoff--Miethe treaty/bank-deposit PPML applications. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolver derived the weighted-cycle nullspace, bounded-score tangent construction, explicit PPML coefficient, canonical gradient, and exact loss. For every cycle it perturbed Cov(Y_gt,Y_gg), obtaining a diagonal balance response -1/(B mu_gt); a positive fixed-support Rademacher density realizes the full q-dimensional covariance family while keeping means and variances fixed, so the loss is an explicit positive-definite quadratic form. Exact rational calculation reproduced the legal 3x3 witness: theta=.5, V*=.06333936, PPML variance=.06506836, and Gamma=.00172900. All 56 staggered supports through T=6 passed independent cycle-basis/response checks. Singular covariances, zero means, absent never-treated support, unrealizable perturbations, generic-GMM collapse, and the additive PT-All quotient collision were checked and excluded or placed outside scope. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the general finite-fourth-moment tangent lower bound with an explicit differentiable-mean submodel convention and justify score-moment differentiation while preserving the bounded-law topology construction. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct every canonical cycle and covariance-response matrix through T=6, verifying the diagonal -1/(B mu_gt) response, unchanged cycle Gram, and exact fixed-support covariances; any failure stops the topology converse. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_ppml_ptt_cycle_efficiency_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Is PPML imputation semiparametrically efficient for every bounded nonnegative-outcome covariance law exactly when the untreated cohort-time bipartite graph is acyclic, and, when its cycle rank is q>0, are the exceptional efficient covariance laws characterized by exactly q primitive alternating balance equations?

source_refs.claim: Introduces proportional staggered-DiD PPML imputation but does not characterize when its Poisson working score is efficient under covariance misspecification.
source_refs.author: Ninon Moreau-Kastler
source_refs.venue: EU Tax Observatory Working Paper 31 / SSRN

source_refs.claim: Develops an algebraic-combinatorial theory of low-rank matrix completion in which observation-graph cycles control local entry relations and completability.
source_refs.author: Franz J. Király, Louis Theran, and Ryota Tomioka

source_refs.claim: Shows that covariance restrictions in multiplicative panel models can create efficiency gains beyond mean-based quasi-likelihood estimation, without a graph-topological criterion.
source_refs.author: Jeffrey M. Wooldridge

source_refs.claim: Shows in additive staggered-rollout designs that optimal estimation depends on outcome covariance and feasible weighting can strictly improve precision.
source_refs.author: Jonathan Roth and Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna

open_problems.why_unsolved: Low-rank matrix-completion work supplies cycle-controlled algebraic relations, while staggered-DiD efficiency work supplies covariance-dependent optimal weighting; the scan found no paper joining them into an efficiency frontier. The missing proof step is to show that weighted alternating even-cycle vectors span the complete linearized restriction space and that equality of the PPML and efficient influence functions is equivalent to one independent covariance-balance condition per primitive cycle. A support-preserving realizability construction is then required to prove that these restrictions are genuinely nongeneric rather than artifacts of an unrestricted covariance calculation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if theorem indexed by q=|U|-|C_U|-|T_U|+1, together with q independent covariance-balance equations for q>0 and an exact nonnegative loss formula Gamma=b'(R'Omega R)^(-1)b with sharp zero and spectral bounds.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its proportional-target and PPML-imputation framing, then turn its unexamined precision question into a topology-level frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Proportional DiD requires a nonlinear imputed counterfactual -> PPML supplies a convenient working estimator -> arbitrary within-unit covariance separates convenience from efficiency -> untreated-graph cycles determine exactly when that distinction matters

method_exemplars.technique: Translate rank-one matrix restrictions into algebraic relations indexed by cycles of the bipartite observation graph and use graph/matroid rank to count independent restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The untreated mean array is a positive rank-one partial matrix, and the desired q-dimensional tangent restriction is the differential counterpart of its cycle relations.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive covariance-dependent optimal staggered-design weights, plug in covariance estimates, and compare asymptotic variances through a positive quadratic form.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed frontier likewise compares a conventional staggered estimator with its covariance-optimal counterpart and requires both an attaining estimator and an exact efficiency-loss comparison.

method_exemplars.technique: Use extra orthogonality conditions implied by nonlinear panel second moments to exhibit efficiency gains over baseline quasi-likelihood scores.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The q cycle balances are covariance-sensitive directions that PPML can fail to exploit.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one prove the semiparametric tangent-space lower bound for proportional treatment on the treated in a fixed-T staggered panel with a positive connected rank-one untreated-mean array, allowing arbitrary within-unit dependence and only finite fourth moments?

source_refs.claim: Provides a probability-limit argument and recommends a unit-resampling panel bootstrap, but contains no tangent-space or efficiency-bound analysis.
source_refs.author: Ninon Moreau-Kastler
source_refs.venue: EU Tax Observatory Working Paper 31 / SSRN

source_refs.claim: Derives semiparametric efficiency bounds for distributions restricted by conditional moments, supplying a generic projection framework but not the nonnegative fixed-T rank-one mean model.
source_refs.author: Gary Chamberlain

source_refs.claim: Develops tangent-score calculations, efficiency bounds, estimator construction, and limit theory without resolving the support-preserving submodel issue for nonnegative outcomes here.
source_refs.author: Whitney K. Newey

open_problems.why_unsolved: Moreau-Kastler establishes consistency of a ratio of observed and imputed means and then invokes a panel bootstrap; it does not specify a differentiable dominated submodel, justify differentiation of cohort-time means through scores, or prove that every allowable linearized mean perturbation is induced by a legal nonnegative law. Chamberlain and Newey provide the abstract Hilbert-space recipe, but the first missing proof step is a bounded-score construction that simultaneously preserves outcome support, finite fourth moments, the rank-one untreated-mean restriction, and arbitrary within-unit covariance.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem defining an explicit differentiable-mean submodel class, identifying its closed tangent space through score-moment equations, and proving a convolution or information lower bound for every regular estimator of theta_PTT.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from nonnegative outcomes and proportional effects to staggered-treatment imputation, then isolate efficiency as the unresolved inferential layer.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Nonnegative outcomes make log-linear percentage effects problematic -> multiplicative parallel trends identify a percent change of the treated mean -> staggered timing motivates PPML imputation -> attainable precision under the mean-only model remains unknown

method_exemplars.technique: Project pathwise derivatives onto the closure of scores satisfying moment restrictions and derive the least-favorable covariance-weighted influence function.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The rank-one untreated means generate a finite moment-restriction model whose sharp variance bound is likewise an orthogonal-projection problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use explicit parametric submodels and score equations to calculate the efficient influence function and establish asymptotic linearity of a plug-in estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result needs exactly the bridge from an abstract tangent restriction to a constructive lower bound and attaining estimator.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the canonical gradient of theta_PTT under the connected multiplicative rank-one untreated-mean restriction, and does a feasible covariance-weighted minimum-distance imputation estimator attain its variance bound under arbitrary within-unit covariance?

source_refs.claim: Defines the proportional target as a ratio of treated observed and imputed counterfactual means and suggests panel-bootstrap inference without deriving an influence function or comparing covariance-weighted estimators.
source_refs.author: Ninon Moreau-Kastler
source_refs.venue: EU Tax Observatory Working Paper 31 / SSRN

source_refs.claim: Derives an efficient imputation estimator and its asymptotic behavior for additive staggered event-study targets with unrestricted treatment-effect heterogeneity.
source_refs.author: Kirill Borusyak, Xavier Jaravel, and Jann Spiess

source_refs.claim: Derives and attains the semiparametric efficiency bound for ATT in canonical additive DiD with panel or repeated-cross-section data.
source_refs.author: Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna and Jun Zhao

source_refs.claim: Shows that second-moment restrictions in multiplicative nonlinear panels imply additional orthogonality conditions that can yield efficiency gains.
source_refs.author: Jeffrey M. Wooldridge

open_problems.why_unsolved: The additive efficient-imputation results do not transfer mechanically: theta_PTT is a nonlinear ratio, its denominator is itself a rank-one extrapolation from untreated cells, and the nuisance mean parameters are coupled across cohorts and times. Under arbitrary within-unit covariance, the optimal projection depends on the full covariance operator, whereas PPML uses Poisson working weights. The first unresolved step is to differentiate the ratio jointly with the rank-one mean manifold and solve the resulting covariance-weighted constrained projection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A closed-form canonical-gradient formula, a feasible estimator using a consistent within-unit covariance estimate, and an asymptotic-linear normal limit with pointwise Wald intervals attaining the semiparametric bound.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation and theorem sequence cleanly separate the causal estimand, robust imputation, efficiency, implementation, and inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Staggered treatment plus heterogeneous effects invalidates conventional regression targets -> clean untreated observations support imputation -> optimal weighting turns imputation into an efficient estimator -> proportional nonlinear targets require the analogous covariance-aware construction

method_exemplars.technique: Solve the efficient-score projection with covariance-weighted moment restrictions and read off the information bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is a smooth finite-dimensional functional of means subject to nonlinear restrictions, so its canonical gradient follows from the same weighted projection geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the untreated outcome model on clean observations, impute treated counterfactuals, aggregate with target-specific weights, and prove asymptotic linearity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest staggered-DiD estimator-and-limit-law template, with the additive target replaced by a ratio and the projection weights replaced by full covariance weights.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit conditional second-moment information in multiplicative panel models through additional orthogonality conditions and efficient moment weighting.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly explains why a Poisson mean score need not exhaust efficiency when the covariance law is unrestricted.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the cycle-rank efficiency frontier for proportional staggered DiD survive when country-pair observations form a separately exchangeable dyadic array rather than independent units, and what replaces the canonical gradient and feasible covariance weighting under shared-country dependence?

source_refs.claim: Applies staggered nonlinear DiD inside a structural gravity model for bilateral trade and reports economically material differences from conventional RTA estimates.
source_refs.author: Arne J. Nagengast and Yoto V. Yotov

source_refs.claim: Uses a balanced quarterly panel of 1,397 country pairs to estimate staggered treaty effects on international bank deposits.
source_refs.author: Lukas Menkhoff and Jakob Miethe

source_refs.claim: Reanalyzes both bilateral applications with proportional PPML imputation and resamples country-pair units, leaving dependence among dyads sharing a country outside its theory.
source_refs.author: Ninon Moreau-Kastler
source_refs.venue: EU Tax Observatory Working Paper 31 / SSRN

source_refs.claim: Shows that multiway-clustered sample means may have non-Gaussian limits and that uniformly consistent limiting-distribution estimation is impossible without additional restrictions.
source_refs.author: Konrad Menzel

source_refs.claim: Establishes empirical-process, nonlinear-estimator, variance-estimation, and bootstrap results for multiway-clustered exchangeable arrays.
source_refs.author: Laurent Davezies, Xavier D'Haultfoeuille, and Yannick Guyonvarch

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two named consumer applications are bilateral panels, so dyads sharing an exporter, importer, residence country, or haven may be dependent even when country pairs are used as nominal clusters. The independent-unit proof's first invalid step is the iid tangent-space and direct-sum covariance projection: under exchangeable arrays it must be replaced by a Hoeffding or Aldous-Hoover component decomposition, and degeneracy can change both rate and limit law. Existing multiway-cluster theory gives generic CLTs and bootstraps but not the canonical gradient or the interaction between dyadic covariance components and the untreated cohort-time cycle space.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A separately exchangeable-array efficiency theorem giving the canonical gradient, convergence-rate regimes, a feasible multiway covariance-weighted estimator and valid confidence procedure, plus a characterization of whether q=0 remains necessary and sufficient for universal PPML efficiency.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates the destination directly through bilateral gravity data, staggered RTAs, PPML, rich fixed effects, and economically material estimator differences.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: RTAs arrive at different dates across country pairs -> heterogeneous effects invalidate conventional staggered comparisons -> structural gravity calls for PPML on bilateral flows -> shared-country dependence requires a dyadic efficiency theory for proportional imputation

method_exemplars.technique: Use exchangeable-array empirical-process decompositions to prove nonlinear-estimator asymptotic normality, consistent multiway covariance estimation, and pigeonhole-bootstrap validity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the dependence-aware asymptotic machinery needed after replacing independent cohort units by bilateral observations.

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose multiway-clustered statistics into projection components, track degeneracy-driven non-Gaussian limits, and use an adaptive bootstrap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A valid frontier must state when the first-order dyadic projection is nondegenerate and what inference remains possible when it is not.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode rank-one mean restrictions by the observation graph and obtain independent local relations from graph cycles.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The mean-restriction side remains graph-indexed even though the sampling covariance changes from iid vectors to an exchangeable dyadic array.

literature_map:
Moreau-Kastler (2025, EU Tax Observatory WP 31/SSRN 5247936) is the exact anchor: it defines PTT as a percent change of the treated mean and proposes staggered PPML imputation.
Its formal inferential content stops at a probability-limit argument and a unit-resampling panel bootstrap; the scan found no asymptotic or efficiency-bound treatment.
Ciani and Fisher (2019, Journal of Econometric Methods, DOI 10.1515/jem-2016-0011) establish the multiplicative-DiD and PPML rationale in the canonical setting.
Wooldridge (2023, Econometrics Journal, DOI 10.1093/ectj/utad016) gives nonlinear staggered-DiD cohort-time effects and pooled/imputation equivalence, but not efficiency for the aggregate proportional ratio.
Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2024, Review of Economic Studies, arXiv:2108.12419) provide the closest additive analogue: robust efficient imputation, asymptotic normality, and inference.
Sant'Anna and Zhao (2020, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.06.003) derive an ATT efficiency bound for canonical additive DiD; Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1803.09015) extend staggered identification and inference.
Roth and Sant'Anna (2023, JPE Microeconomics, arXiv:2102.01291) show that covariance-aware weighting can sharply improve staggered-rollout precision, underscoring that working PPML weights need not be optimal.
Chamberlain (1987, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/0304-4076(87)90015-7) and Newey (1990, Journal of Applied Econometrics, DOI 10.1002/jae.3950050202) supply general tangent-projection and efficiency-bound machinery.
Wooldridge (1999, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/S0304-4076(98)00033-5) specifically shows that second-moment restrictions in multiplicative panels yield extra orthogonality conditions and efficiency gains.
Király, Theran, and Tomioka (2015, JMLR, arXiv:1211.4116) connect rank-one partial matrices to observation-graph algebra and local completion relations; the scan found no paper joining this cycle geometry to causal efficiency.
Santos Silva and Tenreyro (2006, Review of Economics and Statistics, DOI 10.1162/rest.88.4.641) remain the PPML and heteroskedasticity foundation; Chen and Roth (2024, QJE, arXiv:2212.06080) clarify why ratio-of-means targets are attractive with zeros.
Nagengast and Yotov (2025, AEJ: Applied, DOI 10.1257/app.20230089) place staggered nonlinear DiD in structural gravity and find conventional RTA effects biased downward by more than 50 percent in their sample.
Menkhoff and Miethe (2019, Journal of Public Economics, DOI 10.1016/j.jpubeco.2019.06.003) supply the second consumer setting: 1,397 bilateral country pairs and staggered information-exchange treaties.
Those bilateral applications expose a second frontier: Menzel (2021, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA15383) shows multiway-cluster limits can be non-Gaussian, while Davezies, D'Haultfoeuille, and Guyonvarch (2021, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1807.07925) give exchangeable-array CLT and bootstrap tools but no proportional-DiD efficiency result.
